newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- US debt volatilities steady in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- US debt volatilities steady in slow trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were steady in slow morning business as traders returned from a long weekend, dealers said.
The opening of a new bond trading floor at the Chicago Board of Trade today also kept activity in Treasury bond futures options slow and cautious.

"It's a relatively quiet day," said a brokerage trader at CBOT. "It's right after the three-day holiday and there aren't very many numbers (economic indicators). I think a lot of people are doing less business just because they want to make sure they've got everything working okay" on the new floor.
U.S. financial markets were closed on Monday for the Presidents' Day holiday.
Implied volatilities for April and June T-bond futures options shortly before noon were virtually unchanged from Friday's closings at 9.2 and 9.5 percent.
Traders awaited Wednesday's U.S. January consumer price index. They expected it to be relatively market-friendly, given the soft producer prices data last Friday.
Still, many traders expected T-bond futures to be consolidative near term as open interest, which had built up to record levels in recent weeks, looked toppish.
According to final figures released late in the morning, open interest for CBOT T-bond futures dipped 10,730 contracts to 549,550 on Friday after edging up to new highs for days.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were steady to firmer.

"Vols are low enough that people think they're cheap, but they're still a little afraid they can go lower," said an investment bank trader for an investment bank at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options were up about 0.1 point to 8.8 and 12.7 percent respectively.
